modern: If the gods have made decisions about me and about the things which must happen to me, they have decided well, for it is not easy even to imagine a deity without forethought; and as for doing me harm, why should they have any desire for that? For what advantage would come from this to them or to the whole, which is the special object of their providence? But if they have not made decisions about me individually, they have certainly made them about the whole at least, and the things which happen as a consequence in this general arrangement I ought to accept with pleasure and be content with. But if they decide about nothing—which it is wicked to believe, or if we do believe it, let us neither sacrifice nor pray nor swear by them, nor do anything else which we do as if the gods were present and lived with us—but if, however, the gods decide about none of the things which concern us, I am able to decide about myself, and I can inquire into what is useful; and what is useful to every man is what is in keeping with his own constitution and nature. But my nature is rational and social; and my city and country, so far as I am Antoninus, is Rome, but so far as I am a man, it is the world. The things, then, which are useful to these cities are alone useful to me.
original: If the gods have determined about me and about the things which must happen to me, they have determined well, for it is not easy even to imagine a deity without forethought; and as to doing me harm, why should they have any desire towards that? for what advantage would result to them from this or to the whole, which is the special object of their providence? But if they have not determined about me individually, they have certainly determined about the whole at least, and the things which happen by way of sequence in this general arrangement I ought to accept with pleasure and to be content with them. But if they determine about nothing,—which it is wicked to believe, or if we do believe it, let us neither sacrifice nor pray nor swear by them, nor do anything else which we do as if the gods were present and lived with us,—but if however the gods determine about none of the things which concern us, I am able to determine about myself, and I can inquire about that which is useful; and that is useful to every man which is conformable to his own constitution and nature. But my nature is rational and social; and my city and country, so far as I am Antoninus, is Rome, but so far as I am a man, it is the world. The things then which are useful to these cities are alone useful to me.
